citation: 1901 S. Prairie Ave. 'In 1898 as owned by Mr. Ream.' [Norman B. Ream house, from across Prairie Avenue to the south-west.] Unknown photographer, 1898 (the hosting page's caption). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1901 S. Prairie.
author: unknown photographer
date: by 1893 (the same photograph as Rand McNally's 1893 Pictorial Chicago plate); captioned 1898 by Chicagology
repository: chicagology.com (secondary reproduction; the original holder is not named). Prairie library image a19-cgy-1901-ream-1898, recorded there as 'link only'; the project's reference copy is the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a19-cgy-1901-ream-1898.jpg), committed since T-1903 at data/sources/assets/ream_1901_photos_t1903/ with its attribution, as the owner directed on 2026-10-11 for the image gate's pictures.
locator: The whole street front from its north corner to the canted south-west corner, the porch and its balcony, the cornice and the mansard with its dormers; the south flank's front half and its canted bay, seen steeply; the area fence and its gate posts. A street tree stands across the front's south part.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's own ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-1903) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-27 (T-3185, piece 1 of T-1903) from the image store's reference copy, 981 x 673 px greyscale, sha256 86070921794e13ab8816336bd7eec5a65774ed9d313efed15d76820110582892. Dated 2026-10-29 (T-3186): this copy is Rand McNally's 1893 Pictorial Chicago plate cropped (rand_mcnally_pictorial_chicago_1893_ream; fitted image to image by a scale of 1.0049 and a shift, its eight camera-fit points within 0.5 px), so the photograph was taken by 1893; the caption's 1898 can only date Ream's ownership, not the exposure. The library's own range for the plate is 1888-1893.
note: The fullest picture of the Ream house this project builds from. A light smooth ashlar house of two tall storeys over a raised basement: on the front's north part one window column; then a stone porch on paired Corinthian columns with responds at the wall, its flat top a balcony with a stone balustrade before the window over the door, reached by a stoop between curved stone cheeks; south of it one more window column, and the front's south end cut by a canted face with its own window column; every window under a moulded head with a small cornice on consoles; a deep cornice on large paired blocks over a frieze, carried round the south flank; a slated mansard with pedimented dormers over every window column and an iron cresting on its curb; the south flank's canted bay carried through both storeys with its own dormer; an iron fence of scrolled panels on a stone curb, with tall square stone posts.
what_it_supplies: the street front's composition: its window columns, the porch and balcony, the canted south-west corner, the cornice, the mansard and its dormers
the heights of the principal floor, both storeys, the windows, the porch and the mansard through the photograph's camera
the tone of the walls: a light smooth stone
what_it_does_not_supply: the north flank, the rear and the brick rear range
the south flank's rear half, behind the canted bay
